text:
alex: quick flag. tide24b (int4) canary started returning sporadic CUDA OOMs on multi-turn sessions >1024 tokens. rejection rate ~2% on canary-3 this morning. stack traces mention small-chunk alloc failures and high free_slot churn. anyone seen similar? :eyes:

	dana: can you paste the exact error / a short log?

	alex: snippet:```
	2026-03-22T09:12:03Z worker-23 ERROR AllocFailed: cudaMalloc failed (out of memory)
	KVCache: used=42MB chunks=8 free_slots=3	max_new_tokens=512	batch=8	prefetch=on
	callstack: serve -> kv_prefetch -> alloc_chunk
	```

	miguel: smells like fragmentation. int4 reduces static model memory but increases number of small per-token buffers (kv + attn scratch). quick mitigations: set max_new_tokens=256, reduce microbatch target to 4, lower kv_evict_threshold from 0.8->0.6. also propose enabling slot_compactor on a couple canary workers to test compaction of free slots.

	priya: also seeing a minor quality delta on our news summarization eval after int4 quant: ROUGE drop ~1.8 points vs fp16. ran `/evals/run_quality.py --model tide24b --quant int4 --suite news-summ --seed 42` this morning.

	sam: agree with non-revert first. operational plan: reduce defaults for tide24b-int4; for chat routes that are long-context, route to tide24b-int8 automatically if tokens_estimate > 1024. fallback routing avoids user-visible regressions while we tune int4.

	ci-bot: canary deploy note: tide24b-int4 v2026.03.22.08 started on pool-canary-3 (sha=a1b2c3).

	dana: will run local repro with the original multi-turn prompt set. running:```bash
	python tools/repro_oom.py --model tide24b --quant int4 --prompt tests/long_dialog.json --batch 8 --max_new_tokens 512
	```

	priya: kicking off full eval sweeps (int4 vs int8 vs fp16) and will write outputs to gs://redwood-evals/tide24b/2026-03-22/; will include exact metric diffs and sample pairs.

	miguel: enabling slot_compactor on canary-5; leaving canary-6 as control. compaction_interval=60s. will collect memory histograms + free_slot distributions after ~30m.

	alex: plan: (1) dana reproduce and attach heap traces (ETA 2h), (2) miguel patch canary config: max_new_tokens=256, batch.soft_cap=4, kv_evict_threshold=0.6, slot_compactor=on for one worker (ETA 1h), (3) priya run quality sweep and share diffs (ETA 3h). if quality delta >2 pts on primary suites we'll route long-chat to int8. @dana @miguel @priya update thread with artifacts.

	dana: started repro. capturing tracemalloc + nvprof + `python -m tracemalloc` snapshots. will post gists.

	priya: sweep started. filing results to gs://redwood-evals/tide24b/2026-03-22/int4_vs_int8/ and will summarize in Slack when done.

	miguel: initial memory histograms: control (no compactor) shows free_slots churn high variance, compactor worker shows lower peak fragmentation and no OOMs in 30m window. sending charts to thread.

	sam: good signal. if compactor holds we can roll to more canaries and keep reduced max_new_tokens/default microbatch. configured routing rule for long chats to int8 and pushed to canary routing policy.

	alex: thanks. if anyone notices error spike or 5xx increase, @alerts will page SRE. reconvene after priya/dana reports. :thumbsup:

	ci-bot: automated test: canary smoke for tide24b-int4 passed (latency/throughput within expected bounds).

	priya: posted eval summary: int4 vs fp16 on news-summ: ROUGE-L -1.9, ROUGE-1 -1.1, some length truncation artifacts noted with high max_new_tokens. int8 matches fp16 within noise. artifact links: gs://redwood-evals/tide24b/2026-03-22/int4_report.html

	dana: repro traces uploaded: gs://redwood-traces/tide24b/oom_repro/trace_1718234567.zip. nvprof shows repeated small allocations at alloc_chunk called during kv_prefetch, confirming fragmentation hypothesis.

	miguel: next steps: (A) keep int4 for low-latency short requests with reduced defaults, (B) route >1024 token requests to int8, (C) roll slot_compactor to 50% of canaries, (D) open follow-up to revisit quant config per-layer to recover quality. I'll open a PR with the config changes and a rollout plan.

	alex: perfect. please add a quick blurb in the model onboarding doc about "int4 tradeoffs: fragmentation risk for long-context; defaults should be conservative". closing loop once PR merges.

	priya: noted. I'll add eval artifacts and summary to the model onboarding checklist and link to this thread.

	miguel: PR created: r/r/1234 with config and compactor opt-in. tagging for canary rollout tomorrow morning.

	alex: great work team. will follow up if anything changes.
